look_here_first: Start with life cycle and panicle shape. Purple threeawn is a perennial bunchgrass with mostly basal, often tightly rolled leaves and a relatively narrow to sparingly branched panicle. The three long awns are usually subequal and often purplish when fresh.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Hays — Purola Preserve natural flora; Williamson — detailed county treatment of A. purpurea var. purpurea; Travis — USDA ARS herbarium collections from Austin/Travis County.

best_field_traits: three long spreading awns, usually subequal
awns commonly purplish to reddish before drying
morphology_keys.comparison_training: Aristida oligantha is annual, wiry and much more openly branched, with an airy panicle and very long three-awned lemmas.
